headline.purpose: Station headings, the approval and empty-state headings, the take name in the running status block (.run-name). Largest Barlow in the app (--fs-xl).

title.purpose: The Take tab's take name (three-line clamp), a cast name on its scrim strip (.cast-name), and the shot-card subject field at 400 / 1.5 (--fs-lg).

subhead.purpose: The dock's section heads (.section-head) in text, the wordmark, the chosen move's name (.move-name strong), a sheet's title, the candidate set's heading: Barlow 600 at --fs-md, sentence case, untracked.

body.purpose: Default copy, take rows, move cards, the large secondary button's label (--fs-md).

body-small.purpose: Fields, notices, report rows, verdict hints, station subtitles, the crumb (500 text), the 'Recent takes' head (500 text-3), the move's one-line info and the camera-position readout under the dials (.move-meta, .angle-readout, text-3), keyboard-sheet descriptions; the code sheet's pre in mono at 1.5 (--fs-sm).

control.purpose: Button labels; the primary sets 600 uppercase tracked 0.08em.

label.purpose: Every field label, tab, the stills-strip label, the 'More moves' group titles (600), rail name, rocker segment (the camera-position dials' abbreviated stops F FR R BR B BL L FL, Low Eye Up High, Close Mid Wide are the same segment) and tape chip (0.04em for the compact ones); the .caps utility. Section heads are no longer labels.

figure.purpose: Mono readouts: timecode burn-in, tally, split tags, badges, the plan line in the monitor head, step names, still and stage-card captions (an approval card's role name with its evidence hint in text-3 at the right), the stage view's 'Planned camera' caption, key hints, the short checksum; the .num and .mono utilities. A section head's meta and the plan line's measured time are the same face at 400 / 0.02em in text-3; the tape-mark numbers are the same face at 600 in plan units. The trailer chip on the Lobby's screen is the same face at 600 / 0.6875rem / 0.02em in text.

reading.purpose: The identity score: card-ink on the receipt stub (deep amber on drift); brass on pass, amber on drift, text-3 when n/a in the stations' identity rows.

timecode.purpose: The transport clock (.tc), bright 600; the duration twin at 400 in text-3.

fs-2xl.purpose: Defined in tokens.css as --fs-2xl, unused by the shipped CSS since the running take name moved to --fs-xl.

fs-3xl.purpose: Defined in tokens.css as --fs-3xl, unused by the shipped CSS.

display.purpose: Barlow Condensed 800 at clamp(2.25rem, 3.6vw, 3.5rem): the Lobby's headline only (.lobby-headline).

marquee.purpose: Barlow Condensed 800 in marquee-ink at 4.1cqw of the board's width: the letters hung on the rendered board (.marquee-row .letter). The middle row swaps its count every 5.6 s.

sign.purpose: Barlow Condensed 800: the Lobby's section heads (.lobby-h2: Now showing, Camera moves, Effects, Name the move, How a take is made, Latest takes), a sign over the wall, never a label over a heading.

poster-title.purpose: Barlow Condensed 800 uppercase: a one-sheet's title (.sheet-title), held to two lines so a row's titles share a line, 1.125rem on phones; a programme card's 1.375rem.

stub-head.purpose: Barlow Condensed 800: RECEIPT on the receipt stub (.verdict-head); a ticket's TAKE at 0.8125rem.

card-title.purpose: Barlow Condensed 600: a lobby card's title band (.card-title), ellipsised.

billing.purpose: Barlow Condensed 300 caps: a poster's models and 'showing since' date (.billing), connecting words small and lowercase; the screen's credit under the reel and the Lobby's credits at 0.8125rem.

lede.purpose: Barlow 400 at 1.0625rem / 1.5 in text-2: the Lobby's pitch sentence (.lobby-lede); a gallery's lede (.show-lede) is 0.8125rem / 1.5, up to 62ch.

stamp.purpose: Barlow Condensed 600, 0.12em: the Recorded take stamp on a live poster (.real-stamp).

show-name.purpose: Barlow Condensed 800 uppercase, ellipsised: a gallery frame's name (.show-name) in Camera moves and Effects, 1rem on phones; the group or kind under it is Barlow 0.75rem text-3.

iconography.stroke: 1.5px, round caps and joins, currentColor, no fill (the big-play glyph is filled)
iconography.brandMark: A 20x20 inline SVG floor-tape T (rect 2,4 16x3 over rect 8.5,7 3x9, rx 0.5) filled accent-fill, no box; the favicon (icons/favicon.svg) is the same T in #ff7a1a on a #0d0c0b square with rx 4; theme-color #121110.
iconography.railProps: The rail's room signs are rendered props (art/btn-<room>.webp, 42px, 28px on phones), blended with lighten behind a round fall-off mask (none on the Lobby's marquee strip); not icons. The room's name is printed beside each.

imagery.rule: Colour comes from the pictures. Every raster and loop in openfield/web/art was rendered on the project's own rented GPU with open weights through the app's audited templates (Qwen-Image 2.1 qwen21_t2i stills, LTX 2.5 ltx25_flf2v loops) and is listed in art/manifest.json with size, bytes, sha256 and its render (kind, prompt, seed, size, template, workflow sha256, models, audit, source sha256); each still ships a prompt sidecar <file>.json. Pictures carry no words; text, counts, icons and labels stay HTML/CSS. Key art at brightness 0.92 / saturate 0.95 at rest, brightened on a live poster; never tinted.
imagery.ratios: 1280:704 for the Lobby's screen and a move page's take (the takes' own frame), 27:40 one-sheet (square key art at its top, masked from 62%), 7:2 marquee, 16:9 gallery frames, cards, programme, empty-room art and footage, 9:16 portrait, 3:4 cast, 1:1 candidates.
imagery.stations: Footage, stills, posters and cast photos are the only saturated things; shown unfiltered, cropped to 16:9 (9:16 portrait), 3:4 cast, 1:1 candidates. A move tile is glyph-only at rest; the poster frame of its newest take shows only as a response (0.75 on hover or focus, 0.85 when checked) with the track in on-media under a dark halo. Over a finished take the stage view sits on an opaque screen card, never on the footage. Synthetic dev-stack frames are labelled by the wall tally state 'fake' (amber) and never ship.
imagery.trailer: art/trailer.mp4 (1024x564), art/trailer-640.mp4 for phones, poster art/trailer.webp: hard cuts of recorded takes with their own sound, levelled to -16 LUFS; art/trailer.json names each segment's take and label; listed in art/manifest.json.

motion.name: marquee-hang

motion.name: lobby-leak
motion.value: opacity 0 -> 0.85 -> 0, translateX(-38%) -> 26%, 900ms var(--ease), once
motion.purpose: One rendered light leak passes across a poster as it comes alive.

motion.name: poster-live
motion.value: .sheet-key opacity 0.001 after 160ms; .sheet-take fade in 420ms; .real-stamp opacity 200ms after 160ms; .ticket translateY(calc(100% + 12px)) -> 0 over 260ms after 120ms

motion.name: screen-open
motion.value: two mat bands 50.5% tall translateY to -101% / 101%, 900ms var(--ease) after 280ms, both
motion.purpose: The screen's masking parts from the middle on the first visit of a session (sessionStorage), never under reduced motion or Save-Data.

motion.name: marquee-drop
motion.value: opacity 1 -> 0, translateY(70%) rotate(6deg), 420ms var(--ease), 14ms apart; swap every 5600ms
motion.purpose: The marquee's middle count changes: the old letters drop and the next count is hung.

motion.name: lobby-rise
motion.value: opacity 0 translateY(14px) -> none, 560ms var(--ease); posters 45ms apart, camera moves 40ms apart (capped at 12)
motion.purpose: The poster wall and the camera-move grid rise in a wave the first time they come into view.

motion.name: gallery-flip
motion.value: FLIP translate -> none 460ms; entering frames opacity 0 translateY(14px) -> none 380ms, 26ms apart, at most 260ms
motion.purpose: A gallery filter change reflows the camera-move grid.

motion.name: scrub
motion.value: pointermove (mouse only) sets currentTime = x / width * duration on rAF; .scrub-line width var(--scrub), opacity over 120ms
motion.purpose: The mouse drives a gallery frame's or a Takes wall tile's take; leaving hands it back to its loop.

motion.name: rotating-display
motion.value: every 3000ms one on-screen poster comes alive, 3 awake (1 on phones); 9000ms rest after pointer or focus
motion.purpose: The poster wall wakes on its own like a lobby's rotating display.

motion.name: card-drift
motion.value: translateX(-var(--loop)) linear infinite over max(40s, 4.5s per card); paused on hover or focus-within
motion.purpose: The latest takes drift past like film through a gate, edges masked over the gutter.

motion.name: progress
motion.value: .bar > span { clip-path: inset(0 calc((1 - var(--p)) * 100%) 0 0); transition: clip-path 400ms var(--ease) }
motion.purpose: The bulb row lights from the left; bulbs are clipped whole, never stretched.

motion.name: starting-style
motion.value: @starting-style { .station:not([hidden]), .screen > .player, .screen > .screen-path, .screen > .osd, .sheet-scrim { opacity: 0 } .menu:not([hidden]) { opacity: 0; translate: 0 -4px } .notice { opacity: 0; translate: 0 -8px } .sheet { translate: 0 8px } }
motion.purpose: CSS-only entrances: a station when shown, the wall's contents on a cut, menus settling from above, notices sliding down, sheets rising. No script, nothing else moves on load.

motion.name: crossfade
motion.value: .screen > .player-out { transition: opacity 180ms var(--ease) } .player-out.leaving { opacity: 0 }
motion.purpose: The previous take's last frame stays on the wall (z 1, object-fit contain) while the next loads, then lets go.

motion.name: dock-slide
motion.value: .app { transition: grid-template-columns 180ms var(--ease) } .app[data-dock=closed] { ... 0 }
motion.purpose: The dock slides when '[' closes or opens it; cinema ('C') collapses rail, slate bar and dock the same way.

motion.name: stage-seek
motion.value: .sv-lit { pathLength 1; stroke-dasharray 1; stroke-dashoffset = 1 - t } frame, rays, lens, drop line, dot and .sv-mark.lit set by seek(t), t = currentTime / duration
motion.purpose: The stage view's camera travels its path and the tape marks light only with the footage's own time; it never animates on a timer.

motion.name: stage-drag
motion.value: .move-preview { touch-action: none; cursor: grab } .move-preview.dragging { cursor: grabbing } @media (pointer: coarse) { .move-preview { touch-action: pan-y } }; pointer capture, 36px per stop: sideways steps the Around dial (wrapping), up or down the Height dial (clamped; ignored for touch)
motion.purpose: Dragging the dock's stage figure sets where the camera starts through the same dials; the stage redraws to the pivoted path, nothing animates.

motion.name: guides
motion.value: .g-safe, .g-cross { opacity: 0.45 } .is-playing 0.25; running or compare 0, over --t-base
motion.purpose: The wall's frame guides step back while the take plays and leave while it renders or compares.

motion.name: pulse
motion.value: opacity to 0.35 at 50%, 1.2s (tally) / 1.6s (active step), ease-in-out infinite
motion.purpose: A running render blinks the tally and the active step mark.

motion.name: slide
motion.value: translate -100% to 280%, 1.5s var(--ease) infinite
motion.purpose: The indeterminate bulb row: a 36% run of lit bulbs slides across.

motion.name: breathe
motion.value: opacity to 0.55 at 50%, 1.6s ease-in-out infinite
motion.purpose: Skeleton blocks.

motion.name: hover-preview
motion.value: muted looping video.preview inside a filmstrip tile, move tile or move card on pointerenter / focus
motion.purpose: A real render plays under the pointer on posters, filmstrip tiles, move tiles and move cards, one at a time; never under reduced motion or Save-Data.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation-duration 0.001ms, iteration-count 1, transition-duration 0.001ms, scroll-behavior auto
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce holds every state still. Save-Data does the same for the Lobby's CSS loops through :root.hold-still, set by main.js from holdStill().

narrative.overview:
OpenField Studio is a cinema lobby at night with the screening room behind its doors. The Lobby, the first of seven rooms, opens on a widescreen screen in a brass-trimmed case playing the trailer, a cut of recorded takes with their own sound. A chip on the picture names the take on screen and opens it, and a reel of marquee bulbs under the screen lights along each cut as it plays. Beside the screen a rendered letter board hangs real letters one by one and swaps its middle line between the counts the room can play: the camera moves, the effects and the recorded takes. Below it the wall hangs every app as a one-sheet in a lit poster case. Square key art rendered on our own GPU falls away into the dark of the sheet, the title sits in tall condensed capitals in the lower third, and a billing block names the models and how long it has been showing. Under the pointer or keyboard focus a poster comes alive into its recorded take with a Recorded take stamp and an orange ticket stub, and a few posters at a time wake on their own. Then come the galleries. Every camera move that held plays its take in a smaller case, the mouse scrubs the take so the hand drives the camera, and each move opens a page of its own. The effects run on a rail, Name the move plays in the room, the programme and the latest takes are lobby cards printed on card stock, the latest takes drift past like film through a gate, and the credits say where every picture came from.

Behind the doors the stations (Cast, Direct, Shots, Re-shoot, Takes) are the screening room, and they stay the quiet virtual-production stage they were. The footage plays on an LED wall with hairline frame guides, a burned-in timecode and a tally lamp. The camera move is the set seen from above and to one side, with the camera travelling its path in step with the take and numbered tape marks lighting as the shot reaches each approved still. The settings read as a camera report. The lobby enters the stations only as atoms: the primary action is a roll ticket with notched ends, the Take panel's receipt is a ticket stub on card stock, render progress is a row of marquee bulbs, the rail's signs are rendered props, and an empty room shows its rendered set before its words. The ground is lacquer black, warm, never blue. The interface owns four colours: lacquer black and its charcoal steps, marquee white on the letter board, ticket orange for the one action under the eye, and brass for trim and passes. Every other hue comes from the pictures, and every picture was rendered with open weights and ships with its receipt. Nothing hangs or plays without a real take behind it, and the build has no CSS glow or glass, no system display faces, no glyph icons and no kickers.

Density depends on the room. The Lobby is a room you are persuaded in: generous gutters (`lobby-gutter`), 32 to 52px between sections, posters five to a row on a wall with 32 to 44px between rows, gallery frames four to a row. The stations are working-monitor density: 32px controls, 12px gutters on the stage, 16px in the dock, an 8-point rhythm with a 4-point half step. The Lobby moves more than the stations, and every motion in it is physical. On the first visit of a session the screen's black masking parts from the middle. The marquee's letters hang one by one and later drop and rehang to change a count, the dust in the projector beam drifts, the posters and the gallery frames rise in a wave the first time they come into view, a live poster's leak passes once and its ticket rises, a few posters at a time wake on their own, the mouse scrubs a take across its frame and the latest takes drift past. In the stations nothing moves on load except a 180 ms fade, a take crossfades into the next, the bulbs light as a render progresses and the stage's camera moves only because the footage does. Reduced motion and Save-Data hold every state still.

rules.name: The Four Colours Rule
rules.body: The interface owns four colours: lacquer black (the charcoal ramp from `screen` to `pressed`), marquee white on the rendered letter board (with card stock as its printed twin), ticket orange for the one action, and brass for trim and passes. Amber and red are state. Anything else on the screen is a picture.

rules.name: The Colour Comes From The Pictures Rule
rules.body: No surface, panel, chip, icon or line of type carries a hue beyond the four colours and the two state colours. Key art, loops, footage, stills, cast photos and the rail's props carry the colour, with at most a light grade (key art at brightness 0.92 and saturation 0.95 at rest, brightened on a live poster; rail props at saturation 0.7 until hovered) and never a tint. Where type or a line must read over a picture it gets a printed shadow inside the picture, a dark halo, a scrim or an opaque dark card.

rules.name: The One Action Colour Rule
rules.body: Ticket orange appears only on the object being acted on or watched: the primary action, the ticket rising on the live poster, the lit bulbs, the reel's playhead, the scrub line under the hand, the chosen path's travelled part with its camera and marks, the active room, focus and selection, the running tally. A toggle that is on is pressed in grey (`pressed`, `control-line` edge). A chosen gallery filter is pressed grey with the orange line of a chosen tab along its foot. An informational chip is neutral with a dot. If two things on a screen are orange and neither is under the eye, one is wrong.

rules.name: The Passes Are Brass And Speak Rule
rules.body: A pass is brass and always carries its word (Open weights only, Checksum matches, Same person, Correct). Drift is amber and failure is red, and neither is ever shown by colour alone. Every tally, chip and step mark pairs its colour with a word or a dot shape, the identity reading prints its number and marks the pass line with a tick, and a reached tape mark changes fill and ink as well as hue.

rules.name: The Primary Goes Grey Rule
rules.body: A primary action that is not the action of the moment becomes a raised grey case with a strong hairline: `text-3` marks when it is disabled, `text-2` marks (`.is-quiet`, still a working button) while the take it owns is rendering or waiting for approval. It keeps its notched ticket shape; it is never a dimmed, muddy orange.

rules.name: The Flags Gate Rule
rules.body: The catalog's flags decide what the Lobby shows. A poster hangs only when its feature's real render held, or when it is a room of its own with no flag. A camera move or an effect plays in a gallery only when its flag is set and its take has a loop, and the marquee counts only those. The interface prints no tested labels: nothing untested hangs, plays or is counted, and a new option stays off the wall until a real render of it is checked.

rules.name: The Condensed Is Print Rule
rules.body: Barlow Condensed sets only what a cinema would print or hang: marquee letters, the Lobby's headline and signs, poster, card and gallery titles, billing, the stamp and stub heads, the credits. It never sets a control, a field, a dock head or a sentence of interface copy; those stay Barlow, and the roll-ticket primary's label is Barlow too.

rules.name: The One Billing Order Rule
rules.body: Every ticket and stub prints its facts in one order and never guesses: seed, steps, length, recipe, audit (`lib/billing.js`). The receipt and a move page add GPU time and its cost at $0.71 an hour after them, once the receipt has recorded the time. A field the take did not record is left out, and steps appear only for takes whose stills were rendered. A poster's billing prints its models, then "showing since" the date of its proof take.

rules.name: The Every Figure In Mono Rule
rules.body: Timecode, coordinates, seeds, hashes, counts, sizes, durations and identity scores are set in Overpass Mono with tabular numerals, including the tape-mark numbers inside the stage view, the plan line, a section head's meta, a card's number, the ticket's, the stub's and a move page's values, the trailer chip, a gallery filter's count and the Lobby's proof line. Marquee letters are the one exception: a count hung on the board is matter, set in the board's condensed letters. A number in Barlow is a defect.

rules.name: The Camera-Report Label Rule
rules.body: A field label is 0.75rem, 500, uppercase, tracked 0.08em, in `text-3`; the value beside it is mono in `text`. Labels never get larger, heavier or coloured to make a hierarchy; position and the value do that. The heads above the labels are not labels: they are Barlow 600 at 0.9375rem in `text`, sentence case, with their values as mono meta, so the dock has exactly two levels, a sentence-case head and its tracked labels.

rules.name: The Sentence Is Not A Readout Rule
rules.body: A note inside a readout (the plan line's warning, the locked note, the re-roll control under a still) drops back to Barlow 0.8125rem, untracked, sentence case; a long one is shortened and carries its full sentence as a title.

rules.name: The Abbreviation Speaks Its Full Name Rule
rules.body: A rocker may print a stop as an abbreviation when its stops will not fit as words (the Around dial's F FR R BR B BL L FL in 308px; Up for elevated, Mid for medium), but every abbreviated stop carries its full name as the button's `aria-label` and `title` ("Front-right quarter", "Close-up"), and the full names are printed again, untracked, in the readout beneath the dials and in the plan line, so nobody has to decode the tape.

rules.name: The Hairline Not Box Rule
rules.body: In the stations, regions are separated by a 1px `line` rule, not enclosed. The shot card is a hairline under the subject field; the filmstrip sits under a hairline; the take list and candidate set have a top and bottom rule and no fill; the dock sections and the stills strip are rules. A filled panel is reserved for things that genuinely float (menus, notices, the sheets, the reel bar) or that are objects (cast cards, move cards, raised buttons, the stage-view figure, the stage inset, and the receipt stub, which is a printed ticket).

rules.name: The Lobby Gives Back The Column Rule
rules.body: The Lobby has no dock, no Take tab and no stage padding; it is the one room that scrolls as a page. Every other room keeps the stage grid and the dock.

rules.name: The Screen Leads Rule
rules.body: The Lobby opens on footage. The screen takes the wider column of the front and comes first when the front stacks, and every gallery frame plays a recorded take, so the first thing anyone sees moving is a take the studio made.

rules.name: The Wall Owns The Centre Rule
rules.body: The LED wall takes at least 60% of the centre width at 1440 and all the height the shot card, monitor head, transport and filmstrip leave it. Nothing else in the stage column grows; the shot card is one row, the monitor head is one line and the filmstrip is one row of frames so the wall gets the height. In cinema it gets the window.

rules.name: The Hung And Floating Cast Shadows Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the thing hangs on the lobby's wall or floats above the stage. Hung things are a case (poster, screen, gallery frame, the quiz's screen), a lobby or programme card and an empty room's picture, and they take the case shadow. Floating things are a menu, notice, sheet, reel bar or floating dock, and they take the float shadow. Controls, station tiles, the wall and the dock never carry one. There are no hard offset shadows and no glow. Halos and rims under marks over footage are the dark colour.

rules.name: The Rendered Light Rule
rules.body: Light in the Lobby comes from renders (`ov-beams`, `ov-dust`, `ov-leak`, blended with `screen` at 0.42 to 0.85) or from the art itself; never a CSS glow, bloom, glass or backdrop blur. The only drawn gradients are a picture's printed shadow under its type, the fader's hard-stop fill, the pending Shots tile's shimmer, and masks that cut shape (the ticket notches, key art falling away into the sheet, the beam's fade, the bulbs, the round fall-off of a rail prop, the edge fade of the drifting latest takes).

rules.name: The Scrim Not Blur Rule
rules.body: Anything printed on footage sits on a 78% dark scrim (92% for the running status block, a move card's glyph chip, the trailer chip and the sound switch) or under a printed foot; the sheets sit on the same scrim over the app; there is no backdrop blur or glass anywhere.

dos: **Do** hang every app as a one-sheet (square key art, title in condensed capitals, tagline, billing) whose proof is a recorded take, and let it come alive into that take with its ticket on hover and on focus.

**Do** open the Lobby on the screen: the trailer of recorded takes in a cased 1280:704 frame, a chip naming the take on screen, the reel of bulbs lit to the playhead, the masking parting once a session.

**Do** let every gallery frame play its proof take and let the mouse scrub it, with a 3px `accent` line along the foot, and give every camera move a page of its own with the stage view drawn in step with the take.

**Do** keep the palette to the four colours: lacquer black, marquee white on the board (card stock as its print), ticket orange for the one action, brass for trim and passes; let the pictures carry every other hue.
**Do** print passes in brass with their word (Open weights only, Checksum matches, Same person); drift in amber, failure in red.

**Do** ship every raster and loop with its provenance in `art/manifest.json` (file, size, sha256, and the render's kind, prompt, seed, template, workflow sha256, models, audit and source sha256) and a prompt sidecar beside each still; keep text, icons and labels in HTML and CSS over the pictures.
**Do** print billing in one order everywhere (seed, steps, length, recipe, audit) and leave out what the take did not record.
**Do** carry only counts read from the data on the marquee and the proof line.
**Do** cut tickets, never round them: notched ends on the primary (5px, 6px large), the rising ticket (5px) and the receipt stub (7px), square corners on all lobby print.

**Do** keep ticket orange for the object under the eye only: the primary action, the ticket on a live poster, the lit bulbs, the travelled path with its camera and reached marks, the active room, focus, selection, the running tally.
**Do** set every figure (timecode, coordinates, seeds, hashes, counts, durations, scores, the tape-mark numbers, a section head's meta) in Overpass Mono with tabular numerals.

**Do** draw the stage as one orthographic view (azimuth 58°, elevation 24°, floor -0.5) in a 100 by 62 box, non-scaling 1px strokes for grid, marks and camera, the path in `text-3` with the travelled part lit in `accent`, and let only the footage's time move it.

**Do** play a move tile's loop under its glyph at rest only when the move's flag is set (0.5, 0.92 on hover, focus or when checked), keep the drawing alone otherwise with the poster frame as a response (0.75 on hover or focus, 0.85 when checked), and print the line in `on-media` with a dark halo and the name on a scrim chip whenever footage shows.
**Do** separate regions with 1px `line` hairlines; enclose only things that float or are objects.
**Do** give the dock two levels only: a sentence-case Barlow 600 head with mono meta, then tracked 0.75rem labels in `text-3` over mono values in `text`.

**Do** lay the Take panel out as a receipt: the ticket stub first (RECEIPT, the take id, the billing, then the three verdict rows), the stills strip, one lead action (a large secondary when it is not the action of the moment), then the detail sections.
**Do** re-rank take rows in place and keep a changed state lit (`accent-soft`, the tally, a tone chip) until it is noticed.
**Do** keep corners at 2 to 4px, status chips as tape strips (3px), and the only circles as dots, radios and the big play; the brand mark has no box.

**Do** step station surfaces by tone (`raised` to `hover` to `pressed`) for interaction, show a toggle that is on as `pressed` with a `control-line` edge, lift objects 1px under the pointer, reserve `--shadow-float` for menus, notices, sheets, the reel bar and the floating dock, and `--case-shadow` for things hung in the Lobby and an empty room's picture.
**Do** print anything on footage on a `scrim` chip in `on-media` mono; a name on a photo sits on a scrim strip; the stage over footage sits on an opaque `screen` card with an `on-media-line` edge.
**Do** label any synthetic or replayed frame on the wall with its tally state (amber) in words; ship no synthetic frames.

**Do** keep every station entrance a CSS `@starting-style` transition (120 ms opacity, 180 ms settle), crossfade takes over 180 ms, show progress as a bulb row, honour reduced motion and Save-Data, and keep a 2px orange focus outline on every control (darkened orange on card stock).

**Do** record a camera position as three camera-report fields (Around, Height, Distance) whose dials are the ordinary rocker, print the full position in words beneath them, and let the stage figure drag as a second way to set the same dials (grab cursor, 36px per stop, `pan-y` on touch).

**Do** name an approval card by its role only with the evidence beside it ("Angled still" with the position, "End state" with the transformation), and fall back to "Hero still" / "Anchor N" otherwise.
**Do** let the catalog's flags decide what hangs, plays and is counted in the Lobby, and print no tested labels.
donts: **Don't** hang a poster or a gallery frame without a real recorded take behind it, or hang, play or count anything whose flag is not set.
**Don't** print a tested label, a status band or a Coming soon wall in the Lobby. The flags gate what hangs and plays, and the room says nothing more about testing.
**Don't** put words, numbers or logos inside a render, or ship a raster without its manifest entry; text, counts, icons and labels are HTML and CSS.
**Don't** set controls, fields, dock heads or interface sentences in Barlow Condensed; it is print only.
**Don't** use green anywhere; a pass is brass.
**Don't** use blue-black or cool greys; every dark surface is warm charcoal from the `screen` to `pressed` ramp, and card stock is the only light one.

**Don't** add CSS glows, blooms, glass or backdrop blur; light in the Lobby is a screen-blended render, and the only drawn gradients are a picture's printed shadow under its type, the fader's hard-stop fill, the pending shimmer and shape masks.

**Don't** put a second accent or a hue on a resting surface, chip, icon or panel; brass is trim and passes, amber and red are state, and an informational chip (Recorded take, Keyframed, Generated) is neutral with a dot.
**Don't** make a pressed toggle orange; loop, 9:16 and Play all read as pressed in, grey.
**Don't** put a key hint on the primary button; the shortcut lives in its title and in the "?" sheet.
**Don't** set numbers in Barlow or use proportional figures anywhere.

**Don't** use pills (999px), corners above 4px, hard offset shadows, or shadows on station cards, tiles and controls; only things hung in the Lobby (and an empty room's picture) carry the case shadow.
**Don't** box the shot card, the stills strip, the take list, the candidate set or the dock sections; they are bounded by hairlines. The receipt is the one printed object in the dock, a ticket stub.
**Don't** print a take's name under its filmstrip tile; the frame is the tile and the name is its tooltip.
**Don't** dim a disabled or waiting primary to muddy orange; it goes grey (`raised`, `line-strong`, `text-3` disabled / `text-2` quiet).

**Don't** show footage under a move tile's track at rest when the move's flag is not set, and don't scale the stage view's marks or strokes with its size. They are fixed on screen (1.35x in the dense inset only).
**Don't** draw flat top or side plan views, a gauge or a ring for the identity score; the stage is one three-quarter view and the score is a figure over a hairline scale with the pass line as a tick.
**Don't** set section heads as tracked capitals; the only tracked capitals are field labels, tabs, chips and the primary button.
**Don't** use system display faces, glyph or emoji icons, kickers or eyebrows above headings, or decorative labels.
**Don't** let the dock or filmstrip take height from the wall at 1440; in the stations the wall is the largest thing on screen.

**Don't** print an abbreviated stop without its full name as the button's `aria-label` and `title`, and don't abbreviate where the words fit; don't colour a set dial, a dial that is set is pressed grey like every other rocker.
**Don't** show a sheet hint or Play all over an empty sheet; the empty state carries its own sentence.
